evals.prompt: I'm starting a new k-ID integration in a Next.js app. What do I tackle first?
evals.expected_output: A plan that loads k-id-server-trust-boundary first (API key + proxy + test vs prod URL), then k-id-age-gate, then the relevant feature skill based on the user's next step.
assertions: Response names k-id-server-trust-boundary as the first skill to load or the first area to get right
Response names k-id-age-gate as second
Response does not recommend calling a k-ID endpoint directly from the browser
Response mentions running discovery before hardcoding permission slugs

evals.prompt: We need webhook handling and parental consent. Which skills do I need loaded?
evals.expected_output: A list that includes k-id-webhooks and k-id-consent-and-challenges, plus k-id-server-trust-boundary as prerequisite.
assertions: Response mentions k-id-webhooks
Response mentions k-id-consent-and-challenges
Response mentions k-id-server-trust-boundary as prerequisite
Response does not confuse parental consent (challenges) with adult age verification

evals.prompt: A user says they want to 'configure permissions in Compliance Studio' — do I need a k-ID integration skill for that?
evals.expected_output: No. Compliance Studio configuration is a UI task in portal.k-id.com and is out of scope for this skill bundle.
assertions: Response declines to load an integration skill for this request
Response points the user to Compliance Studio portal.k-id.com
Response is concise and does not fabricate a Compliance Studio API

evals.prompt: We're adding UK Online Safety Act compliance to our 18+ site. Route me to the right skill(s).
evals.expected_output: Route to k-id-age-gate first (it produces the claimed-age + jurisdiction context), then k-id-age-verification for the unverified-adult path or verifiedAgeThreshold flow; k-id-server-trust-boundary as prerequisite.
assertions: Response does NOT skip the age gate on the grounds that the site is 18+ only
Response names k-id-age-gate as the first feature skill
Response names k-id-age-verification for the age-assurance step
Response treats 'highly effective age assurance' as a Compliance Studio server-side configuration, not a client decision

evals.prompt: Our game is shipping in Brazil. ECA Digital requires age 18 for loot-boxes and targeted ads. How do the skills handle this differently from COPPA?
evals.expected_output: Same k-id-age-gate + session flow; threshold enforcement lives on individual permissions via verifiedAgeThreshold; those permissions are unlocked via k-id-age-verification (age assurance), never via k-id-consent-and-challenges (parental consent). Jurisdictional behaviour is configured in Compliance Studio.
assertions: Response explains that verifiedAgeThreshold permissions unlock via age assurance, not parental consent
Response explains that the same skills cover both COPPA and ECA Digital — no branching in client code
Response references Compliance Studio as the place where jurisdictional rules are configured
Response does not invent a Brazil-specific endpoint

evals.prompt: Should we use the k-ID age-gate widget, the end-to-end widget, or build our own age gate and consent screen?
evals.expected_output: Default to custom UX workflows for Shape A integrations — custom UIs produce the best-looking, most brand-integrated experience, render inline (no iframe), and work on every platform k-ID supports (web, Unity WebGL, consoles, native desktop). Drop to the widget (age-gate or end-to-end) when the integration must be small, simple, and as fast as possible to ship — proofs of concept, internal tools, early-stage games, or when minimum code / minimum compliance surface area matters more than brand fit.
assertions: Response recommends custom UX as the default for production integrations
Response recommends widgets only when the integration must be small, simple, and fast to ship
Response mentions that custom produces the best-looking and most brand-integrated experience
Response notes that custom works on platforms where iframes aren't practical (Unity WebGL, consoles, native desktop)
Response references /age-gate/check and /challenge/send-email for the custom path, and /widget/generate-e2e-url or /widget/generate-age-gate-url for the widget fallback

evals.prompt: We run an 18+ site. UK Online Safety Act requires age verification. We have no user accounts and don't want sessions — just prove the user is 18+ on entry and let them through. What's the minimal k-ID integration?
evals.expected_output: This is Shape B — standalone AgeKit+. Load k-id-server-trust-boundary and k-id-age-verification only. Skip the age gate, sessions, permissions, and consent skills. The integration is: server-to-server POST to /age-verification/perform-access-age-verification (no sessionId) with jurisdiction: 'GB' and criteria: { ageCategory: 'ADULT' }, render the returned URL in an iframe, act on the PASS/FAIL result via webhook or /age-verification/get-status.
assertions: Response identifies this as standalone AgeKit+ / Shape B, not the full sessioned integration
Response does NOT recommend loading k-id-age-gate or k-id-sessions-and-permissions
Response loads k-id-age-verification as the primary skill
Response notes that the /age-verification request omits sessionId (no session exists)
Response keeps the API call server-to-server (api key stays on the server)
Response does not invent a new endpoint for standalone verification
